authorship.note: third-party coverage mentioning Nimrod Dvir ('Nimrod Dvir of Maariv' in a party guest list); not a sample of his writing.

completenessChecks: All nine gossip items translated in order; the single hyperlink ('we reported') kept on the same words.
Both captions translated with credits and kept before the paragraphs they precede, as in the Hebrew capture.
Every name in the guest lists is present; none dropped or merged.
voiceChecks: Gossip-column register kept: clipped items, 'Wedding season 1 / 2' labels, the dry joke about the guest who arrived a day late, the sign-off pun on Hadas Rivak's trip.
No narration added to explain who the people are.
decisions: Column title 'התחתית' rendered 'The Bottom Line' (the Hebrew literally 'the bottom' is the column's name; the APA line keeps the captured literal gloss 'The bottom').
'בקרוב אגיע רחוק' rendered 'Soon I'll go far', keeping the item's wordplay on the name Rivak/far.
The first caption keeps the source's misspelling 'רנית' as 'Ranit' because the Hebrew capture preserves both spellings; the subtitle and body use 'Ronit'.

Show and outlet names use established English forms where they exist (Beauty and the Geek, Big Brother, The Amazing Race, MasterChef, Calcalist, Israel Hayom, Yedioth Ahronoth); 'HOT Bidur Yisraeli' and 'Café Telad' are transliterated.
sourceProblems: Spelling inconsistency רונית / רנית in the source, retained (see decisions).
'הזוג' spellings and the dash in the subtitle ('לקשת- "התחתית"-') are typographic in the source and normalized to a colon in English.
unresolvedQuestions: Whether the archive needs this item on the website; Nim is only a name in a guest list.
